title: Marguerite Bourgeoys (12 January)
hookLine: a pioneer teacher in early Montreal, founder of an uncloistered community

lines: A TINY SETTLEMENT IN THE FOREST.
cards: A stone stable, empty of animals, swept out. A woman from France stands in it, looking at the walls.
Outside is a tiny settlement on an island in a wide river: wooden houses, a fort, forest in every direction, winters she has never imagined. There are only a few children in the whole place.
She is going to teach them anyway, here, in this stable. The settlement will become Montreal.

teach.b: Marguerite Bourgeoys grew up in Troyes, in France. As a young woman she felt drawn to God, and to teaching, and she joined a group of laywomen who taught poor girls in her town.
The governor of the little French settlement of Ville-Marie, on the island that would become Montreal, came looking for a teacher, and she crossed the ocean with him.

teach.h: A SCHOOL IN A STONE STABLE.
teach.b: In the settlement she was given a stone stable, and she opened a school in it. But she wanted more than one classroom. She wanted women who would teach wherever they were needed, and that raised a problem.
In her day, the Church usually expected women's religious communities to be cloistered: enclosed behind walls, praying, not traveling.
Marguerite took her model from Mary in the Gospel of Luke, who, after the angel's visit, went to help her cousin Elizabeth.

teach.h: MARY WHO SET OUT IN HASTE.
teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "And Mary rising up in those days, went into the hill country with haste into a city of Juda." A Mary who walked out the door. So her community, the Congregation of Notre-Dame, was uncloistered.
Its sisters lived among the people, taught children, trained young women arriving from France to make homes in a hard new place, and went where the need was.
Church authorities were cautious at first, and approval took patience. Saint John Paul the Second declared her a saint.

teach.h: MARY WENT INTO THE HILL COUNTRY WITH HASTE.
teach.b: She started with a stable and a handful of children.

how: Catholics remember Saint Marguerite Bourgeoys in January, especially in Montreal and in schools of the Congregation of Notre-Dame, whose sisters still teach and serve without a cloister.

games.q: you're Marguerite. you want sisters who can teach anywhere, but women's communities are expected to stay behind walls. what do you build your community on?
o: the usual rule of an enclosed convent.
Mary, who set out in haste to help Elizabeth.
games.why: she took Mary on the road as her model and founded an uncloistered community, the Congregation of Notre-Dame.

practice: Think of one thing you know how to do well, a recipe, a shortcut on a phone, a way to fold a shirt, a word in another language, a prayer, and picture one person who might want to learn it.
Imagine showing them simply, the way Marguerite started, with whatever room you have. If you pray, ask for patience as a teacher; if not, just hold that person and that small lesson in mind.

wordCard.voice: Marguerite Bourgeoys. A teacher from France who opened a school in a stable in early Montreal and founded the uncloistered Congregation of Notre-Dame. Remembered in January.
